question: A rectangle has a length 3 m more than its width and a perimeter numerically equal in value to its area. The integer part of the value of its diagonal is:
solution:
**Given:**

The perimeter of the rectangle = The area of a rectangle.

**Formula used:**

Diagonal = √(lenght)² + (breadth)²

**Solution:**

Let the breadth of the rectangle = x 

So the length of rectangle = x + 3

According to the given conditions;

Perimeter = Area

⇒ Perimeter of the rectangle = 2(length + breadth)

⇒ Area of the rectangle = (length × breadth)

⇒ 2(x + 3 + x) = (x + 3) × x

⇒ 2x + 6 + 2x = x² + 3x

⇒ x2 - x - 6 = 0

⇒ x2 - 3x + 2x - 6 = 0

⇒ x(x - 3) + 2(x - 3) = 0

⇒ (x - 3) × (x + 2) = 0

⇒ x = 3 and x = (-2)

So, x = 3 then Length = 6

Diagonal = √(lenght)2 + (breadth)²

⇒ Diagonal = √(6)2 + (3)²

⇒ Diagonal = √45

⇒ Diagonal = 6.7

Diagonal = 6 ( integer part)

Hence option (2) is the correct.
